identity.name: Eastern Hungarian Kingdom
alt_names: Kingdom of Hungary under John I and John II

land.text: Transylvania, held by John Zápolya as voivode, and the eastern part of the kingdom he secured at the Treaty of Nagyvárad (1538)

predecessors.note: Cliopatria starts the Eastern Hungarian Kingdom in 1529, the year John I swore fealty to the sultan (19 August 1529); the page gives the period as 1526 to 1570 and John's coronation on 11 November 1526.

land.text: Transylvania and the Partium, which the Treaty of Speyer (16 August 1570) left to John Sigismund Zápolya

successors.note: Infobox of the Principality: 'Preceded by: Eastern Hungarian Kingdom'. John II died in 1571 and the Báthory came to power; Cliopatria draws this kingdom to 1571 and the Principality of Transylvania from 1572.

capitals.name: Buda
capitals.note: Infobox: Buda (1526-41). The Kingdom of Hungary (1526-1867) page gives Buda for 1526-1536 in its own infobox. Coordinates are those of the gazetteer's Budapest.

capitals.name: Lippa (Lipova)
capitals.note: Infobox: Lippa (1541-42). Coordinates are not on the page.

capitals.name: Gyulafehérvár (Alba Iulia)
capitals.note: Infobox: Gyulafehérvár (1542-70). Coordinates are not on the page.

rulers.name: John I (John Zápolya)
rulers.note: Proclaimed 10 November 1526 at the Diet of Székesfehérvár, crowned 11 November 1526; died at Szászsebes on 22 July 1540 (John Zápolya page).

rulers.name: John II (John Sigismund Zápolya)
rulers.note: Born 15 July 1540. Regents: his mother Isabella and Bishop George Martinuzzi. Abdicated in 1551 and left for Poland; recalled by the Transylvanian nobles in 1556; renounced the kingship at Speyer in 1570 and was recognised as prince of Transylvania and the Partium until his death in 1571.

correction.text: Transylvania, under Zápolya's control from the proclamation of 10 November 1526; the whole kingdom was claimed by both kings and is drawn as contested (see the 1527 and 1538 events)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria starts in 1529. The John Zápolya page has him proclaimed king on 10 November 1526, Ferdinand's army driving him 'from the country by 1528' (EHK page) and his flight to Poland in 1528; it gives no boundary for 1526-1528. Transylvania is the page's statement that Transylvania and the eastern Hungarian plain were under Zápolya control, the only land it assigns to him for these years; unverified for 1527-1528. Reopened in the repair pass: the Zápolya page again gives no boundary; it has him 'voivode of Transylvania', his forces 'tied up in the southern counties of Hungary' in 1527, the pro-Habsburg soldiers capturing Buda, and his flight to Poland in 1528, and does not mention a Partium or a county list for 1526-1529. Transylvania stays an inference.

correction.text: unchanged shape, right for 1529-1537 only: Transylvania, the part of the kingdom John held before the Treaty of Nagyvárad

keyframe_review.note: Cliopatria's 57,163 km2 shape (Romania only) is Transylvania. The Kingdom of Hungary page dates the division to 1538: 'John I secured the eastern part of the kingdom', so the 1538-1539 years take the 1540 shape (keyframe _1538). The page gives no area; the 'reduced by around 60 per cent' remark concerns the whole kingdom.

correction.text: the eastern part of the kingdom that John I secured under the Treaty of Nagyvárad (24 February 1538)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria's growth of 33,130 km2 (131 cells, 21.2-24.8 E, 45.1-48.7 N, all drawn in its Kingdom of Hungary in 1539) comes in 1540, two years after the treaty the page dates 1538. The page does not list the counties; the page says the 1540s kingdom included counties such as Békés, Csanád, Arad and the Temesköz (EHK page).

89,943 km2, 1540-1546: Transylvania and the eastern part of the kingdom after the death of John I (22 July 1540). Cliopatria does not draw Buda in this shape although the page has Buda as the capital to 1541 and says Suleiman took central Hungary as 'Budin Province' in 1541; its Buda cells are in the Kingdom of Hungary to 1546 and the Ottoman Empire from 1547, and this dossier leaves them there.

correction.text: unchanged shape, right for 1547-1550 only: the kingdom before Isabella's cession of Transylvania; 1551 takes the keyframe _1551

keyframe_review.note: 144,466 km2: Cliopatria adds 52,856 km2 (209 cells, 19.9-23.9 E, 45.1-49.0 N, the Kingdom of Hungary's in 1546) in 1547. The page lists Békés, Csongrád, Arad, Csanád and the Temesköz in the 1540s kingdom and has a map 'around 1550' but dates no acquisition; the 1547 year is Cliopatria's (the year its Kingdom of Hungary row ends). No infobox area on any page.

correction.text: the kingdom holds no land: on its dissolution in the summer of 1551 'much of its territories, including the Temes County and the surrounding regions' were integrated into the Habsburg Kingdom of Hungary

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for 1551, drawn empty. The Temeşvar Eyalet page: 'Upon the initial dissolution of the Eastern Hungarian Kingdom in the summer of 1551, much of its territories, including the Temes County and the surrounding regions, were integrated into the Habsburg Kingdom of Hungary', and an Ottoman invasion followed in the autumn of the same year. The Eastern Hungarian Kingdom page: Isabella was compelled in 1549 to sign the Treaty of Nyírbátor, which 'ceded Transylvania to Ferdinand'; 'John II abdicated as king, and together with Isabella left for Poland'; a Habsburg army under Castaldo 'marched into Transylvania and the Tisza region'. No page names any land that stayed with the kingdom ('much of' is not 'all', and the page names the Temes County only as an example), so none is drawn. The first pass kept the Partium and the Temesköz in the kingdom here, which the Temeşvar page, habsburg-monarchy ledger 11 (July 1552, Temesvár lost to the Ottomans) and ottoman-empire ledger 77 contradict.

correction.text: the kingdom holds no land for 1552-1555: John II had abdicated in 1551 and the nobles recalled him only in 1556 (keyframe _1556 takes over)

keyframe_review.note: 112,572 km2 as Cliopatria draws 1552-1555: the 1547 outline less 124 cells (31,360 km2) that Cliopatria gives to the Ottoman Empire in 1552 (Temesvár fell on 26 July 1552, Temeşvar Eyalet page). That land was Habsburg, not this kingdom's: the page has Temes County and the surrounding regions integrated into the Habsburg Kingdom of Hungary in 1551 (habsburg-monarchy ledger 11 and ottoman-empire ledger 77 agree). Cliopatria also keeps Transylvania and the rest in the kingdom throughout 1551-1555, whereas the pages have it dissolved in 1551 (Eastern Hungarian Kingdom page: Nyírbátor 1549, abdication 1551, Castaldo's troops withdrawn in 1553, John II recalled in 1556). The shape is therefore not used for 1552-1555 and the kingdom is drawn empty.

112,322 km2, 1556-1563: Transylvania recalled by its nobles ('In 1556 the nobles of Transylvania recalled John II, and elected him Prince of Transylvania at the Diet of Szászsebes') plus the Partium side of the kingdom, without the Temesköz that the Ottomans held from 1552. The page names Transylvania and lists no other land regained; the whole outline is the land of the 1556 gain (ledger, confidence 2). The Partium page (opened in the repair pass) says the Zápolya house controlled the region 'from 1541 or 1542' and has no event for 1551 or 1556.

correction.text: unchanged shape, right for 1564-1570; the Treaty of Speyer of 16 August 1570 ended the kingdom, and the shape continues in the Principality of Transylvania

keyframe_review.note: Same 112,322 km2 outline as 1556-1563; no change is dated 1564, so the split looks like a data artefact. The Principality of Transylvania page makes the Treaty of Speyer (16 August 1570) the Principality's start and the kingdom its predecessor; John II died in 1571 and Cliopatria draws this kingdom to 1571 and the Principality from 1572, a 1571 overlap or gap for the Transylvania dossier to settle.

region.text: Transylvania, which the page puts under Zápolya control together with the eastern Hungarian plain

ledger.note: 10-11 November 1526: John Zápolya is proclaimed and crowned King of Hungary. 'On 10 November 1526, Zápolya had himself proclaimed king at the Diet at Székesfehérvár' by the lesser nobles, crowned the next day. Ferdinand is elected by the magnates at Pozsony on 17 December 1526, so the country has two crowned kings. The region is the base the page gives him (Transylvania), not a boundary.

region.text: the whole kingdom, claimed by both rivals

ledger.note: July 1527: Ferdinand's German mercenaries enter Hungary against Zápolya, who is beaten at Tarcal near Tokaj on 27 September 1527; Ferdinand is crowned at Székesfehérvár on 3 November 1527 and, by 1528, drives John from the country (he flees to Poland). The two kings contest the kingdom of 1526 until the 1538 treaty.

region.text: the whole kingdom, claimed by both rivals

ledger.note: 24 February 1538: the Treaty of Nagyvárad ends the contest. 'In 1538, the two sides signed the Treaty of Nagyvárad, which made this division official' and made Ferdinand heir to the childless John; the Kingdom of Hungary page: the Habsburgs got 'the northern and western parts of the country (Royal Hungary)', John I 'the eastern part'.

region.text: the eastern part of the kingdom that John I secured at Nagyvárad: Cliopatria's 1540 shape less its 1529 Transylvania

ledger.note: 1538: John I secures the eastern part of the kingdom at Nagyvárad. 'Temporary territorial division between the rival rulers John I and Ferdinand I occurred only in 1538, under the Treaty of Nagyvárad.' Cliopatria draws the 33,130 km2 transfer in 1540 and the page lists no counties, so the region is the Cliopatria difference.

1541: the capital moves from Buda to Lippa after Suleiman takes central Hungary as 'Budin Province' (infobox: Buda 1526-41, Lippa 1541-42, Gyulafehérvár 1542-70); the page says 'In 1541, Ferdinand invaded to enforce his claim' and that Suleiman expelled him and took central Hungary as 'Budin Province'. Buda is not drawn as this kingdom's land by Cliopatria; see notes.
1542: the capital moves from Lippa to Gyulafehérvár (Alba Iulia), where it stays to 1570 (infobox).

region.text: the lands the page lists in the 1540s kingdom (Békés, Csanád, Arad and the Temesköz) with the Tisza lands to the north: Cliopatria's 1547 shape less its 1540 shape

ledger.note: 1547: Cliopatria adds the lands the page lists in the 1540s kingdom (counties such as Békés, Csongrád, Arad, Csanád and the Temesköz; the first pass left Csongrád out of this list). The page dates no acquisition, so the year is Cliopatria's (its Kingdom of Hungary row ends 1546); the counterpart is the Kingdom of Hungary because its 1546 shape holds the 52,856 km2. The Partium page, opened in the repair pass, has no 1547 event and a different county list (Máramaros, Közép-Szolnok, Kraszna, Bihar, Zaránd, Arad, Szörény, Kővár), so the date stays Cliopatria's and the confidence 1.

region.text: much of the kingdom's territory, including Temes County and the surrounding regions, with Transylvania and the Tisza region

ledger.note: Summer 1551: the kingdom is dissolved and its land passes to Ferdinand. The Temeşvar Eyalet page: 'Upon the initial dissolution of the Eastern Hungarian Kingdom in the summer of 1551, much of its territories, including the Temes County and the surrounding regions, were integrated into the Habsburg Kingdom of Hungary', which provoked an Ottoman invasion. The Eastern Hungarian Kingdom page: Transylvania ceded to Ferdinand by the Treaty of Nyírbátor (1549), John II abdicated and left for Poland with Isabella in 1551, and a Habsburg army under Castaldo marched into Transylvania and the Tisza region. The region is Cliopatria's whole 1547 shape (144,466 km2); confidence 2 because the page says 'much of', and names no land that stayed. Ferdinand's realm is the Habsburg Monarchy in Cliopatria from 1547; the matching gain (with Temes County) belongs in habsburg-monarchy.

region.text: Transylvania, which the nobles recalled John II to, with the Partium side of the kingdom: Cliopatria's 1556 shape

ledger.note: 1556: John II is recalled. 'In 1556 the nobles of Transylvania recalled John II, and elected him Prince of Transylvania at the Diet of Szászsebes.' Ferdinand had withdrawn Castaldo's troops in 1553. The page names Transylvania only and lists no other land regained; the region is Cliopatria's 1556 shape (Transylvania and the Partium side of the kingdom, without the Temesköz and Banat that the Ottomans held from 1552); confidence 2.

16 August 1570: the Treaty of Speyer ends the Eastern Hungarian Kingdom. 'In 1570, John II signed the Treaty of Speyer with Ferdinand's successor, Maximilian', renouncing the kingship, 'thus ending the Eastern Hungarian Kingdom'; the land becomes the Principality of Transylvania, a vassal of the Ottoman Empire under the Hungarian crown in public law (Principality page).

wars.name: War between John Zápolya and Ferdinand of Habsburg for the Hungarian crown

zones.text: the whole kingdom, claimed by both rivals

wars.outcome: Zápolya beaten at Tarcal (27 September 1527) and exiled to Poland in 1528, restored in 1529 with Ottoman help after becoming a vassal of Suleiman; the 1538 Treaty of Nagyvárad divided the country, the east to John I, the north and west to Ferdinand.
wars.note: No Wikipedia article for the war is among the pages opened; the name is descriptive. Peace of 1533: 'the Ottomans made peace and ceded western Hungary to Ferdinand' (Zápolya page, undated detail).

wars.name: Ferdinand's invasion and the Ottoman occupation of central Hungary
wars.outcome: Ferdinand invaded in 1541 to enforce his claim after John I's death; Suleiman expelled him, recognised John II as king and his vassal, and took central Hungary as Budin Province.
wars.note: The central territories (Ottoman Hungary) are not drawn as this kingdom's land in Cliopatria; the capital moved to Lippa.

wars.name: Struggle for Transylvania between Isabella, Martinuzzi and Ferdinand

zones.text: Transylvania, ceded to Ferdinand in 1549, and the Tisza region, entered by Castaldo's army; recalled to John II in 1556

wars.outcome: Isabella ceded Transylvania at Nyírbátor (1549); Martinuzzi's army besieged Gyulafehérvár in 1550 and 1551; John II abdicated in 1551; Castaldo's troops left in 1553; the nobles recalled John II in 1556.
wars.note: The zone was Transylvania only in the first pass; the Eastern Hungarian Kingdom page has the Habsburg army marching into 'Transylvania and the Tisza region', and the Temeşvar Eyalet page has much of the kingdom integrated into Habsburg Hungary in the summer of 1551.

certainty.note: The Treaty of Nagyvárad (1538) and the Treaty of Speyer (1570) are not described by lines; the kingdom is Transylvania and counties on the Tisza plain, and the Hungarian-Ottoman frontier moves with each campaign.

notes: Eastern Hungarian Kingdom, eu-15-i, 5 pages (budget up to 5). (1) Life: the lead gives 1526 to 1570; the infobox has the coronation of 11 November 1526, fealty to the sultan on 19 August 1529 (Cliopatria's first year) and the Treaty of Speyer of 16 August 1570 'thus ending the Eastern Hungarian Kingdom'. Cliopatria runs 1529-1571; 1571 (John II's last year) belongs to the Principality of Transylvania dossier, whose Cliopatria row starts 1572. (2) Ottoman vassalage: John I swore fealty to the sultan on 19 August 1529 (infobox; 'Vassal state of the Ottoman Empire') and, in 1541, Suleiman 'recognized John II as king and his vassal'. This is a vassal_start / vassal_end for counterpart eastern-hungarian-kingdom in the Ottoman Empire ledger (me-10), not recorded here; the seed has no relation for it. It ends when the Principality begins (1570), which the Principality page also calls an Ottoman vassal. (3) What Cliopatria's shapes did: 1540 adds the eastern part (33,130 km2, drawn in the Kingdom of Hungary until 1539), 1547 adds 52,856 km2 more from the Kingdom of Hungary's 1546 shape, 1552 gives the Banat side (124 cells, 31,360 km2) to the Ottoman Empire (that land was Habsburg since the summer of 1551 per the Temeşvar Eyalet page, so it is not this kingdom's loss), 1556 and 1564 do not change. (4) Discrepancies: the EHK page says Buda was the capital 1526-41, the Kingdom of Hungary page 1526-1536; John I's son was born 'nine days' (EHK page) or seven days (Zápolya page, 15 July) before his death on 22 July 1540; the principality page puts the Báthory 'upon the death of John II in 1571'. (5) The pages leave open who held Transylvania in 1527-1528 (the dossier uses it as the base) and what, if anything, of the kingdom stayed outside the Habsburg handover of 1551 ('much of its territories'); the repair pass draws the kingdom empty for 1551-1555. (6) Buda and the central plain: Cliopatria draws them in the Kingdom of Hungary to 1546 and the Ottoman Empire from 1547, so the capital Buda is not drawn as this state's; the Kingdom of Hungary and Ottoman Empire dossiers should carry the Ottoman gain of 1541 (Budin Province). (7) Gazetteer: all names used resolve ('Transylvania' region, Cliopatria shapes). 'Partium' is Crisana in the gazetteer; the pages do not define it. (8) No infobox area on any page, so the factor-of-two check could not be made; Cliopatria's 144,466 km2 at the 1547-1551 peak is about a third of the Kingdom of Hungary of 1526 (324,832 km2). (9) Counterparts: kingdom-of-hungary (Cliopatria row to 1546), habsburg-monarchy (Ferdinand's realm from 1547), ottoman-empire, principality-of-transylvania; none needs a new dossier. The Jagiellon tie (John's wife Isabella Jagiellon, married in early 1539; John fled to Poland in 1528 and John II in 1551) belongs to the House of Jagiellon dossier. (10) Repair pass of 2026-10-25 after the reviewer's fail (Temeşvar Eyalet, Eastern Hungarian Kingdom, John Zápolya and Partium pages reopened; the Partium is a sixth page against a budget of 5). The Temeşvar Eyalet page puts Temes County and the surrounding regions in the Habsburg Kingdom of Hungary from the summer of 1551, so the 1552 loss to the Ottoman Empire (old ledger 8) and the 1552 war entry were removed (the Ottoman capture of Temesvár on 26 July 1552 is habsburg-monarchy ledger 11 and ottoman-empire ledger 77). Ledger 7 (1551 loss to habsburg-monarchy) now covers Cliopatria's whole 1547 shape at confidence 2; keyframes _1551 and _1552 draw the kingdom empty for 1551-1555 (an empty region spec: the shape minus itself); the 1556 gain covers Cliopatria's whole 1556 shape (Transylvania and the Partium side), confidence 2, since the page names Transylvania only. Disagreement kept: 'much of its territories' is not 'all', so a small remainder may have stayed with the kingdom; no page names one. Thin items: 1547 (ledger 6) stays Cliopatria's date at confidence 1 (Partium page has no 1547 event, and the EHK page's county list includes Csongrád); 1526-1528 extent stays Transylvania by inference (Zápolya page gives no boundary). For the orchestrator: habsburg-monarchy (eu-09) needs the 1551 gain of the kingdom's land (Transylvania, the Tisza region and Temes County) and the 1556 loss; its 1572 gain names eastern-hungarian-kingdom after that state's end in 1570 and should name principality-of-transylvania.
